title: Understanding Why Foundation Models Work for Diffusion-Generated Image Detection
usefulness_reason: Provides insights into the interpretability and feature-level characteristics of diffusion image detectors (specifically regarding frequency localization and distributional discrepancies).
research_problem: Understanding the underlying reasons behind why vision foundation models work effectively as feature extractors for detecting AI-generated images.
key_findings: Discriminative cues exploited by foundation-model-based detectors are mainly localized in the low-to-mid frequency range rather than just high frequencies.
Regenerated images exhibit reduced variance and effective dimensionality, indicating that diffusion models do not fully reproduce real data variability.
Foundation-model-based detectors succeed by capturing non-semantic low-to-mid frequency distributional discrepancies.
